## How it works

connector.databricks does not handle credentials itself. Authentication is
done by two packages, which look for credentials in your environment:

* [brickster](https://databrickslabs.github.io/brickster/) is used by
`ConnectorDatabricksSQL` and `ConnectorDatabricksVolume`. It is also used by
`ConnectorDatabricksTable` for reading, writing, listing and removing tables.
* [odbc](https://odbc.r-dbi.org/) opens the DBI connection of
`ConnectorDatabricksTable` with `odbc::databricks()`.

| Connector                   | brickster | odbc |
|-----------------------------|-----------|------|
| `ConnectorDatabricksSQL`    | Yes       | No   |
| `ConnectorDatabricksVolume` | Yes       | No   |
| `ConnectorDatabricksTable`  | Yes       | Yes  |

Both packages follow
[Databricks unified authentication](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/unified-auth)
and read the same environment variables. Set them once and you do not need to
pass credentials in code. `ConnectorDatabricksTable` needs both packages to
authenticate, so use a method that both support.

## Environment variables

| Variable                                              | brickster | odbc | Used for                                                       |
|-------------------------------------------------------|-----------|------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `DATABRICKS_HOST`                                     | Yes       | Yes  | Workspace URL, e.g. `https://<workspace>.cloud.databricks.com` |
| `DATABRICKS_TOKEN`                                    | Yes       | Yes  | Personal access token                                          |
| `DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID`, `DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET`    | Yes       | Yes  | Databricks service principal (OAuth M2M)                       |
| `ARM_CLIENT_ID`, `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET`, `ARM_TENANT_ID` | Yes       | No   | Azure service principal                                        |

`DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID` is not a credential. connector.databricks uses it as
the default `warehouse_id` of `connector_databricks_sql()`.

## Working locally

Put the variables in an `.Renviron` file, for example with
`usethis::edit_r_environ("project")`, and restart R. Keep this file out of
version control.

### Personal access token

A [personal access token](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/pat)
is the simplest option and works for every connector:

```
DATABRICKS_HOST=https://<workspace>.cloud.databricks.com
DATABRICKS_TOKEN=<your-token>
DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID=abc123
```

Databricks marks personal access tokens as legacy and recommends OAuth instead.

### OAuth sign-in

To sign in with your own Databricks account, set only `DATABRICKS_HOST` and
sign in in one of two ways:

1. Let brickster open a browser to sign in the first time it makes a request.
This only works in an interactive session on your own machine, and only covers
`ConnectorDatabricksSQL` and `ConnectorDatabricksVolume`, or
2. Sign in once with the
[Databricks CLI](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/cli/authentication).
This works for every connector, including `ConnectorDatabricksTable`. Install
the CLI and run this in a terminal:

   ```sh
   databricks auth login --host https://<workspace>.cloud.databricks.com
   ```

   odbc uses this sign-in directly. For brickster, set
   `options(use_databrickscfg = TRUE)`, and select the profile created by
   `databricks auth login` with `options(db_profile = "<profile>")` if it is
   not your default profile. See
   [Connect to a Databricks Workspace](https://databrickslabs.github.io/brickster/articles/setup-auth.html)
   in brickster for details.

### Service principal

For scheduled jobs and CI, use a service principal with an OAuth secret. Both
packages support it:

```
DATABRICKS_HOST=https://<workspace>.cloud.databricks.com
DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID=...
DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET=...
```

Azure service principals (`ARM_*`) are only supported by brickster, so they do
not work with `ConnectorDatabricksTable`.

## Posit Workbench

With
[Workbench managed Databricks credentials](https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/user/posit-workbench/managed-credentials/databricks.html),
select a workspace under **Session Credentials** when you start a session.
Workbench sets `DATABRICKS_HOST` and `DATABRICKS_CONFIG_FILE`, which both
brickster and odbc detect, and refreshes the token for you. You only need to set
`DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID` if you want a default warehouse.

Do not set `DATABRICKS_HOST` or `DATABRICKS_TOKEN` yourself in these sessions,
for example in `.Renviron`. brickster ignores them when Workbench credentials
are active, but odbc gives `DATABRICKS_TOKEN` priority, so
`ConnectorDatabricksTable` could end up using two different identities. To use
your own credentials, start the session with `None` selected.

## Posit Connect

brickster does not use the Posit Connect OAuth integrations. Set the
credentials as
[environment variables](https://docs.posit.co/connect/user/content-settings/#environment-variables)
of the content instead: `DATABRICKS_HOST` with either `DATABRICKS_TOKEN` or a
service principal's `DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID` and `DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET`. This
works for all connectors.

odbc can use the Connect
[Databricks OAuth integrations](https://docs.posit.co/connect/user/oauth-integrations/)
when the connectcreds package is installed, for example to let a Shiny app query
as its viewer. This only applies to the odbc connection of
`ConnectorDatabricksTable`. Its reads and writes still go through brickster, and
run as the identity in the environment variables above.

## Passing credentials in code

Prefer environment variables, because they are picked up by every connector and
by both packages. If you need to pass credentials directly, use `...`:

```{r in_code, eval=FALSE}
# Passed to brickster::DatabricksSQL() and used for all operations
con_sql <- connector_databricks_sql(
  warehouse_id = "abc123",
  catalog = "my_catalog",
  schema = "my_schema",
  host = "<workspace>.cloud.databricks.com",
  token = my_token
)

# Passed to odbc::databricks() only. brickster still uses the environment
con_table <- connector_databricks_table(
  http_path = "/sql/1.0/warehouses/abc123",
  catalog = "my_catalog",
  schema = "my_schema",
  workspace = "https://<workspace>.cloud.databricks.com",
  uid = "token",
  pwd = my_token
)
```

`host` for brickster must not include `https://`. `ConnectorDatabricksVolume`
has no credential arguments and always uses the environment.

## Checking your setup

* `brickster::db_sql_warehouse_list()` lists the SQL warehouses you can use. If
it works, brickster is authenticated.
* `DBI::dbConnect(odbc::databricks(), httpPath = "<http-path>")` does the same
for odbc.
* `cannot find token or initiate OAuth flow` comes from brickster. It found no
token or service principal, and could not open a browser sign-in because the
session is not interactive or is on a server.
* `Failed to detect ambient Databricks credentials` comes from odbc. None of
the methods above were found.
